# Implement the Music System defined by the Audio Design Chapter

## Goal

Build the runtime background-music system for AI Hell against the fixed design contract captured in
`docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` (produced by **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)**).

User story: *As a player, I want a dynamic, retro-arcade soundtrack that responds to combat intensity, so
that runs feel like the relentless survival experience the game is aiming for; and as a developer I want the
music engine driven by a documented parameter/state contract, so behaviour is testable and reproducible.*

> **Scope stance:** this is **future scope, out of MVP** (GDD §8). The MVP ships baked ToneForge SFX only
> (GDD §7.3), and §7.3 remains authoritative for SFX. This item must **not** be started until the design
> chapter exists and has been reviewed, and it must **not** promote music into the MVP without an explicit
> producer decision.

## Background

- AI Hell currently has **no background music** by design: GDD §7.3 keeps music out of MVP scope, and the
  player-fire grid is deliberately quantised to a **silent internal 80 BPM beat** (AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B).
- SFX are build-time baked WAV assets rendered deterministically by ToneForge and played through Phaser's
  shared `AudioContext` (`src/audio/effects.ts`); the authoritative cue catalogue is
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`.
- The Audio Design Chapter specifies the musical identity (Phrygian Dominant combat scale, Lydian ambient
  scale, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), instrumentation palette, dynamic-mixing rules, state-driven
  transitions, parameter mapping, audio budget and accessibility requirements.

## Expected behaviour and outcomes

- A music system that plays layered/stemmed music driven by an explicit game-state parameter, with
  bar-boundary transitions, stingers, and ducking, as specified by the chapter.
- Music state follows gameplay (e.g. menu/attract, wave combat, boss, low-health tension, run end) with the
  transition rules and timings given in the chapter, and never disrupts the beat grid or the SFX mix.
- Reproducible, deterministic behaviour suitable for automated tests; no audio regressions to the shipped SFX
  pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Contract traceable to the chapter:** every implemented music state, transition, stinger and mixing parameter traces to a named section of `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`, recorded in a mapping table in the implementation docs.
- [ ] **AC2 — Musical content matches the documented identity:** the delivered cues/stems use the chapter's scales, motifs and progressions (Phrygian Dominant combat, Lydian ambient, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), verified by an explicit audit table (motif → scale degrees → usage state).
- [ ] **AC3 — State machine implemented and tested:** transitions occur only at the documented boundaries (bar boundaries unless a stinger cut-in is specified), with unit tests covering each transition in the chapter's transition matrix, including invalid/reset paths.
- [ ] **AC4 — Dynamic mixing implemented:** ducking, per-layer volume targets and the priority tiers behave as specified; SFX intelligibility is preserved (music ducks under key SFX cues) and is covered by tests.
- [ ] **AC5 — Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.
- [ ] **AC6 — Budget met:** the shipped music respects the chapter's audio budget (memory, streaming, polyphony, layer count) on the supported targets, measured and recorded.
- [ ] **AC7 — Docs updated:** GDD §7.3 and §8 are updated to reflect the shipped music system, and `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` is marked as implemented for the sections that ship.
- [ ] **AC8 — No SFX regression:** the existing ToneForge baked-SFX pipeline and cue catalogue remain unchanged and their tests pass; any chapter §6.4 procedural SFX recipes are explicitly **not** adopted unless decisioned separately.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project build and test suite pass.**

## Constraints

- **Blocked by** the docs item **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — this item
  must not begin before `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` exists.
- Music stays **out of MVP scope** until a producer decision promotes it (GDD §7.3, §8).
- Keep the gameplay SVG/vector aesthetic and retro-arcade palette of the chapter; UK English in all docs.
- §7.3 (baked ToneForge SFX) remains authoritative for SFX; the chapter is an addendum whose §6.4 procedural
  SFX recipes are design reference only.
- Prefer reusing the existing audio plumbing (`src/audio/effects.ts`, shared `AudioContext`, manifest-driven
  playback) over introducing new runtime dependencies; any middleware adoption (the chapter's FMOD/Wwise
  guidance) is a separate decision — the web build currently has no middleware.

## Approach (indicative)

1. Confirm scope with the producer (MVP vs post-MVP) and record the decision on this item.
2. Ingest the chapter into an implementation mapping table (state → parameter → cue/stem set → transition).
3. Decide the delivery mechanism (baked stems via ToneForge + `AudioContext` playback, per the existing
   pipeline) versus a runtime synthesiser; record the trade-off before coding.
4. Implement the music state machine and mixing layer behind a single facade, mirroring the existing SFX
   façade style; add unit tests per transition and per mixing rule.
5. Add accessibility controls and the autoplay guard; verify budget and measure on target hardware.
6. Update GDD §7.3/§8 and the chapter's implemented-sections marker.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` — the design contract (prerequisite)
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — existing SFX façade / shared `AudioContext` plumbing to reuse
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — where combat-state music parameters would be driven from
- `src/core/rules.ts` — game-rules config (including `beatBpm`) that music tempo must stay coherent with
- `src/audio/` — new music module + tests
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 and §8 updates

## Risks & assumptions

- **Overlap with the shipped silent beat grid (medium):** player fire is quantised to an internal 80 BPM beat.
  Music must be tempo-coherent with that grid or the two will fight; assume music tempo is either locked to
  `beatBpm` or documented as intentionally independent.
- **Chapter/SFX divergence (medium):** the chapter's §6.4 procedural SFX recipes differ from the shipped baked
  catalogue; §7.3 stays authoritative (AC8).
- **Middleware assumption (low):** the chapter's FMOD/Wwise guidance is forward-looking; no middleware exists in
  the web build, so it is design intent only.
- **Scope creep into MVP (medium):** music is out of MVP; promotion needs an explicit producer decision.

## Related work

- **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — prerequisite; produces the design contract.
- discovered-from:AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W
- GDD §7.3 (SFX, authoritative for MVP), GDD §8 (Future Scope — "Background music"), and
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` (SFX cue catalogue).
- Beat grid / timing context: AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B (beat-aligned fire grid), AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3 (beat-timed
  explosion accents).

## Goal (tracer-bullet vertical slice)

Ship the first end-to-end music slice: the menu/attract ambient track ("Star Drift", Lydian) played through the existing shared AudioContext, driven by a minimal music state machine, with the autoplay/gesture guard and an independent music volume control.

This slice cuts through every layer — baked asset, playback facade, state machine, scene wiring, settings, tests, docs — so later slices extend a proven path rather than a horizontal layer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The menu/attract state plays the baked "Star Drift" Lydian ambient stem as a seamless loop.
- [ ] Music starts only after a user gesture, honouring the AudioContext resume discipline (GDD 7.3), and reuses the single shared AudioContext owned by the playback provider.
- [ ] Music volume and mute are independent of SFX and persisted in the settings record.
- [ ] The state machine enters and leaves the menu/attract state only at a bar boundary of the shared beat clock.
- [ ] Unit tests cover stem looping, the gesture guard, independent volume routing and the menu/attract transition; all playback degrades to a safe no-op without an AudioContext.

- [ ] Covers parent AC5: **Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.

1. Bake the "Star Drift" ambient stem via the ToneForge pipeline and add it to the cue/stem manifest (smallest slice of the stem pipeline).
2. Add src/audio/music/musicPlayer.ts (facade) and a minimal src/audio/music/musicStateMachine.ts with the menu/attract state.
3. Wire gesture-driven start/resume through MenuScene using the shared AudioContext.

## Problem

Candidate D's *States* section (`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § Candidate D → States) defines a ring win as **all six hexes held and the AI's massed counter-attack on the hangar repelled**, and a campaign loss as **the hangar falls** (the last hex taken and the hangar's own defence failing). The MVP build (AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE) deliberately ships the narrower rule, decided by the producer on 2026-10-30 (intake question Q2 = a):

- **Ring secured = every hex of the current ring held.** The next ring then opens.
- **No massed hangar assault** is resolved or played.
- **No hangar-falls lose state**: the hangar itself can never be lost in the MVP, so a player cannot lose the campaign.

## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want the ring to end with a real fight for the hangar — a massed AI counter-attack I have to repel, and a defeat condition that means the hangar can actually fall — so that holding the whole ring feels like a victory rather than the start of the next checklist.

## Desired change

- When the last hex of a ring is captured, **resolve an algorithmic hangar assault** from stored numbers (defender ratings of the held ring vs. the AI's massed force scaled by frontier aggression) — no live simulated battle, matching Candidate D's algorithmic-resolution rule.
- A repelled assault = the ring win state (existing) **plus** a legible report of the numbers.
- A failed assault = **the hangar falls**: define the consequence (restart the current ring with the hangar's unlocks kept, or a documented alternative) and make the reset legible in the defence report.
- Record the chosen win/lose semantics in GDD §8 and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`.
- Pure resolver logic, exercised in the existing `GymHexWar` gym; gym↔game parity per AGENTS.md; attract mode must not stall (no live battle).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Capturing the ring's final hex triggers an algorithmic hangar-assault resolution from stored numbers, with a report showing the numbers that produced the result.
2. A repelled assault marks the ring won; a failed assault applies the documented hangar-falls consequence.

## Problem

`scripts/evaluate.mjs --tune` edits a tracked balance CSV in place and journals the pre-edit bytes beside it (`src/data/<file>.tune-journal`). Both paths are process-global, not per-run:

1. **Startup reconcile steals a live journal.** `main()` reconciles `<csv>.tune-journal` before anything else (crash recovery). A journal is written before the edit and removed after the restore, so it exists for the whole candidate sweep of a *running* process — a second `--tune` run on the same CSV reconciles it, restoring the CSV underneath run 1.
2. **Two runs interleave edits.** Run 2 writes its own journal over run 1's, then restores from run 2's bytes while run 1 continues its candidate sweep against a file run 2 may have rewritten.

Discovered while fixing AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS: the `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` watchdog case asserted "no `*.tune-journal` anywhere in `src/data`", which failed when a sibling suite in the same parallel Vitest run held a journal at the same shared path. The suite was fixed for the shared path (the assertion is now scoped to the run's own pid), but the product-level hazard remains for real concurrent CLI invocations.

## Impact

Two designers (or a designer plus a scripted tuning sweep) tuning the same balance CSV at once can silently produce a comparison against the wrong CSV bytes, and the crash-recovery journal can be consumed by the wrong run. Single-run usage is unaffected.

## Suggested approach

Pick one, cheapest first:

- **Lock file**: an exclusive `<csv>.tune-lock` (O\_EXCL) held for the whole run, with a bounded wait and a clear exit-2 diagnostic naming the holder pid. The journal's pid is already recorded, so the holder is identifiable.
- **Refuse concurrent runs**: on `writeJournal`, if a journal exists whose pid is alive (`kill(pid, 0)`), abort with exit 2 naming that pid instead of overwriting it.
- **Per-run temp CSVs**: out of scope — `--tune` deliberately edits the tracked file so the candidate sweep reads it through the shared config store.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Two concurrent `--tune` runs on the same CSV cannot interleave: the second either waits (bounded) or exits non-zero with a diagnostic naming the holding pid.
2. A live journal is never reconciled by another process: crash recovery only consumes a journal whose pid is dead.
3. `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` and `scripts/csvEditJournal.test.ts` still pass, including the pid-scoped journal assertions added by AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS.
4. `docs/BALANCING.md` documents the concurrency rule alongside the crash-safe journal section.
5. Full suite passes (`/skill:test`).

## Related work

- discovered-from:AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS (the test-failure item that surfaced the shared-path race).

# Mini-Boss "yellow pulse" leaves artefacts

## Problem statement

The mini-boss's expanding yellow pulse wave leaves visible residue: as the ring grows it degrades into a thick, blurry/pixelated band, and a wave that is superseded by the next pulse is frozen on screen at the outer edge of its travel instead of disappearing. The player reports this as "artefacts at the edge of its range" and finds it distracting.

> Original report: "The leel 2 (I think) mini-boss has a yellow pulse that radiates outward. This pulse leaves artifacts at the edge of its range, this becomes distracting. Remove the artifacts"

## Users

Players fighting a boss or mini-boss whose phase set includes the `pulse` pattern (shipped Boss phase 3; Mini-Boss levels 1, 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10).

- As a player, I want the pulse to read as one clean expanding ring so I can judge when it reaches me and dodge it, instead of being distracted by residue.
- As a player, I want each pulse to fade out cleanly at its range limit, with no frozen or ghost ring left on the screen.
- As a player, I must not see a permanent yellow band or ring that outlives the wave that produced it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When a new pulse wave spawns while an earlier wave is still in flight, the earlier wave's sprite is destroyed; at most one live pulse-wave sprite exists per boss at any time (regression test asserts the display list contains exactly one wave sprite after firing two volleys inside one wave lifetime).
- The pulse wave is removed from the display list when it leaves its range, and when the boss is destroyed, with no orphaned wave sprites left behind (regression test asserts zero wave sprites after the wave exits range and after boss defeat).
- The expanding ring renders crisply at every radius up to off-screen: its stroke width does not grow with the radius and no pixelation or stair-stepping is visible (automated assertion on the rendered wave representation — constant stroke width and a native-resolution bake — plus a recorded manual visual check in the gym).
- The wave achieves a smooth fade to zero at the range limit rather than popping out, and the fix does not change pulse gameplay: one wave per volley, aimed-shot count/spread/speed, telegraph cadence, wave expansion speed and collision damage are unchanged (existing Boss and MiniBoss tests pass unchanged).
- Pulse-wave behaviour is identical in `PlayScene` and every gym scene that runs the shared boss tick (gym↔game parity; the fix lives in shared code, not a per-scene copy).
- At least one new or extended automated test covers the wave lifecycle (supersede, range exit, boss destroy) and the constant-stroke render path.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Players no longer see a lingering or blurry yellow ring after the mini-boss pulse, so the wave telegraphs cleanly and the screen stays readable during the fight.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity** (`AGENTS.md`): the fix belongs in the shared `Boss` entity and the shared `CombatScene` boss tick so the game and every gym run the same wave code; no forked copy.
- **Performance** (`AH-0MW2DAY2L004QSKF`): the wave must not reintroduce per-frame re-triangulation of many bullet graphics; the wave is one object and must stay a single cheap draw (or the measured equivalent).
- **Determinism**: no changes to RNG use, `tick(dt)` determinism or wall-clock dependence.
- **Scope**: visuals and wave lifecycle only — no difficulty, HP, cadence or damage tuning.
- **Tests**: run through the test skill (`/skill:test`); no ad-hoc test commands.

## Existing state

- `Boss._spawnPulseWave` (`src/entities/Boss.ts:903`) bakes the `ring` shape **once** at `BOSS_CORE_GLOW_RADIUS = 30` with a 3 px stroke into an ~80×80 texture (`ensureBulletTexture`), then `advancePulseWave` (`Boss.ts:932`) scales that sprite by `_pulseWaveRadius / 30` — up to ~37× on a 1920×1080 screen. A 3 px stroke magnified 37× becomes a ~110 px soft band with visible stair-stepping/pixelation: the ring's edge is the reported artefact.
- **Single-slot wave state:** `_spawnPulseWave` overwrites `_pulseWaveGraphics`/`_pulseWaveRadius` without destroying the previous sprite. When a volley fires while a wave is still in flight, the earlier sprite is orphaned — it stays on the display list, frozen at its last scale/alpha, i.e. a permanent yellow ring at the edge of the wave's range. Wave lifetime exceeds the 1.2 s `BOSS_ATTACK_INTERVAL`, so supersede is routine in a `pulse` phase.
- The wave is destroyed on boss `destroy()` (defeat cleanup, `AH-0MVH85XXZ008INE2`), but that only covers the *current* slot, not an already-orphaned ring.
- **Related defect found (tracked separately):** the wave is advanced twice per frame — `Boss.update` calls `advancePulseWave` and `CombatScene._advanceBoss` calls it again — so it expands at ~600 px/s rather than the documented 300 px/s. This does not itself cause the artefacts, so it is recorded as a discovered work item rather than folded into this fix (see Related work).
- The wave colour is the yellow core colour `BOSS_CORE_COLOR = 0xffff00`, shared by the shipped Boss and every Mini-Boss `pulse` phase — hence "yellow pulse" regardless of the mini-boss body colour.

## Desired change

- Make the wave lifecycle explicit and leak-free: exactly one live wave per boss; destroy a superseded wave immediately; destroy on range exit and on boss destroy.
- Render the ring at native resolution so the stroke stays thin and crisp at every radius (for example a per-frame stroked circle at constant line width, or a ring baked for the maximum radius and drawn unscaled with a fade), while keeping the wave a single cheap draw.
- Keep the fade smooth to zero at the range limit so the wave never pops out.
- Add regression tests for supersede, range exit and boss destroy, plus the constant-stroke render policy.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — `_spawnPulseWave`, `advancePulseWave`, wave state fields and the `destroy` path.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — shared `_advanceBoss` tick (wave ownership) if the fix touches the call site.
- `src/entities/Boss.test.ts` — wave lifecycle, supersede and constant-stroke tests.
- `src/utils/bulletTextures.ts` / `src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts` — only if a full-resolution ring texture (or a new ring draw path) is introduced.
- `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` — update the note that the Boss pulse wave is "a sprite of the cached `ring` texture grown by scale and faded by alpha".

## Assumptions

- **A1 — which boss:** the report says "level 2", but no level-2 Mini-Boss design has a `pulse` phase; the yellow wave is the shared `Boss` pulse code, so the fix is made once in shared code and benefits every `pulse` phase (level 1 "Pulse Warden" phase 2, level 3 "Shard Matron" phases 1 and 3, plus levels 5, 6, 8, 9, 10).
- **A2 — what "artefacts" covers:** both (a) the blurry/pixelated edge of the grown ring and (b) the frozen stale ring left behind when a wave is superseded. Both are treated as artefacts and removed; neither is a tuning change.
- **A3 — no gameplay change:** wave expansion speed, damage and cadence are unchanged by this item. The separately tracked double-advance bug (`AH-0MW9MN4ZO009GFKW`, see Related work) will restore the documented 300 px/s when it is fixed and is explicitly out of scope here.
- **A4 — render approach is the implementer's choice**, provided the stroke stays constant at all radii, the wave remains one cheap draw and the visual identity (yellow ring expanding from the boss) is preserved.

## Risks

- **Performance regression:** a naive per-frame `Graphics` circle redraw is exactly what `AH-0MW2DAY2L004QSKF` removed; the fix must stay within the measured budget of one sprite draw (verify with the perf sweep if the wave path changes materially).
- **Parity drift:** patching only `PlayScene` would diverge the gyms; the repo-wide duplicate-body guard and gym-parity docs assertion will fail if a forked copy appears.
- **Scope creep:** the double-advance and any other pulse-wave tuning discovered on the way are recorded as separate work items, not folded in.
- **Visual verification gap:** "no pixelation" is partly a judgement call; the item must record a manual visual check (gym scene) alongside the automated constant-stroke assertion.

## Related work

- `AH-0MW2DAY2L004QSKF` — cached bullet textures: replaced the per-frame pulse-wave `Graphics` redraw with the scaled cached-ring sprite that produces the blur (source of artefact (a)).
- `AH-0MUII3E5E006A93F` — shared `_advanceBoss` tick, which introduced the duplicate `advancePulseWave` call.
- `AH-0MVH85XXZ008INE2` — "Graphics from mini-boss left behind": fixed the *defeat* cleanup (destroy the current ring on the lethal blow). This item covers the mid-fight supersede leak and the rendering quality, which that fix does not.
- `AH-0MV822FHN005PK37` — Boss pulse projectile identity (the aimed pulse *rings* fired alongside the wave; unchanged here).
- `AH-0MVCRAYSH0014BQJ` — config-driven Mini-Boss framework (phase pattern sets).
- `AH-0MVCC8XSS007P01Z` — parent epic that introduced the mini-bosses.
- `AH-0MW9MN4ZO009GFKW` — Pulse wave expands twice per frame (double `advancePulseWave` call): discovered during this intake, recorded separately (`discovered-from:AH-0MW80W5ER005E884`) so this item stays scoped to the artefacts.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Which boss/level shows the artefact?** — Answer (code inspection, no blocking question): the yellow wave is `Boss`'s shared pulse wave (`BOSS_CORE_COLOR = 0xffff00`), used by the shipped Boss phase 3 and every Mini-Boss `pulse` phase. Level 2's design (`spiral`, `combined`) has no `pulse` phase, so the level in the report is approximate; the fix is in shared code. Evidence: `src/waves/miniBossDesigns.ts`, `src/entities/Boss.ts:903`.
- **Q: What exactly is the artefact?** — Answer (code inspection + report wording "at the edge of its range"): two defects in the same wave path — the 37× magnified 3 px ring stroke (blurry/pixelated band at the outer edge) and the single-slot sprite that orphans a superseded wave (frozen yellow ring at its last radius). Both are addressed. Evidence: `Boss.ts:903-951`.
- No blocking questions for the producer; assumptions A1–A4 are recorded above and are safe to confirm during planning.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUWGD0R5005S4ZD** – P4 ranged pulse effect path, ring VFX, retire BombNotice (completed)
- **AH-0MVCRBISU006NUN5** – PlayScene mini-boss integration (completed)
- **AH-0MVD2N6AW0073X5M** – Wormhole glow/pulse ring (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mv822fhn005pk37, 0mvcc8xss007p01z, acceptance, add, advance (+355 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mv822fhn005pk37, 0mvcc8xss007p01z, acceptance, add, advance (+336 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0muii3e5e006a93f, 0mv822fhn005pk37, 0mvcc8xss007p01z, 0mvcraysh0014bqj, 0xffff00 (+318 more)

# Extra Life adaptive probabilities — Intake Brief (AH-0MW8178ZR0090CNY)

## Original request (verbatim)

> Create a minor increase in the probabiliyt of an extra life power up being dropped as the player loses lives. It should not be noticable, but the player should "feel lucky" when one drops and they are low on lives. This, presumably means the amount of increase is exponential as the player drops to only 1 life left. Also ensure that a mini-boss kill *always* leaves an extra life power up.

> **Status of this brief:** intake is paused pending producer answers to the
> OPEN QUESTIONS in the Appendix. The Acceptance Criteria below are
> **provisional** — they encode the recommended interpretation and tunable
> defaults so the producer has something concrete to approve or adjust. The
> item is marked `needsProducerReview` and its stage is **not** advanced.

## Problem statement

Extra Life currently drops at one fixed rate for the whole run, regardless of
how many lives the player has left. A player down to their last life therefore
gets no extra recovery help, and the moment an Extra Life appears never feels
like a lucky break. Separately, defeating a bespoke mini-boss — the biggest
scheduled highlight of every level — never leaves a life on the field, so the
encounter has no guaranteed survivability payoff.

## Users

- **Players** — want a subtle, invisible-to-them safety net that makes an Extra
  Life feel like a lucky break exactly when they are low on lives, and want a
  mini-boss kill to reliably restore a life.
- **Designers / balance tuners** — need the adaptive curve and the mini-boss
  guarantee expressed as named, persisted tunables (not scattered magic
  numbers) so the feel can be retuned without code changes.
- **Developers / AI agents** — need the rule defined once in the shared core so
  the game and every gym cannot drift apart (gym↔game parity).

### Example user stories

- As a **player on my last life**, I want an Extra Life to drop a little more
  often than usual, so I get a genuine chance to turn a doomed run around —
  without ever noticing the game is helping me.
- As a **player who just beat a mini-boss**, I want the wreck to always leave
  an Extra Life, so the hardest fight in the level reliably pays back a life.
- As a **designer**, I want the adaptive curve in one tunable place so I can
  soften or sharpen the "lucky" feeling without touching gameplay code.

## Acceptance Criteria (provisional — see Appendix)

- [ ] **AC1 — Adaptive mechanism (one shared rule):** Extra Life drop
      probability scales with the player's remaining lives through a single
      pure helper consumed by both `PlayScene` and every drop-bearing gym.
      At or above the run's starting lives the multiplier is exactly the
      current fixed rate (1.0×); it is monotonically non-decreasing as lives
      fall.
- [ ] **AC2 — Shape is exponential and subtle:** the multiplier grows
      exponentially per life lost, reaching a materially higher value at 1
      life. Recommended default: `multiplier = base ** livesLost`, with
      `livesLost = max(0, startingLives − currentLives)` and a base of ~2.5–3
      (i.e. ≈1.0× at 3 lives, ≈2.5–3× at 2 lives, ≈6–9× at 1 life). At 2 lives
      the increase is modest ("not noticeable"); at 1 life it is a clear but
      still small uplift.
- [ ] **AC3 — Statistically verifiable:** a seeded simulation (e.g. N ≥ 10 000
      representative kills per lives value) demonstrates that the Extra Life
      drop rate at 2 lives and 1 life strictly exceeds the full-lives baseline
      and follows the documented curve within tolerance; the test does not
      depend on a single lucky seed.
- [ ] **AC4 — Mini-boss always drops one:** every mini-boss defeat spawns
      exactly one `extra_life` field pickup at/near the mini-boss death
      position, **in addition to** the existing spin-the-wheel reward, in
      `PlayScene` and `GymMiniBoss`. The normal drop separation nudge applies;
      the existing six-slot collection gate and the 5-life cap still govern
      pickup (a drop at the cap is simply not useful, but is still spawned).
- [ ] **AC5 — Tunables + persistence:** the curve constants (starting lives
      reference, exponential base, any cap) live in `GameRules` with documented
      defaults, clamped on load, and older rules blobs load unchanged. The
      existing level-scaling supply dial (`powerUpDropChance` /
      `extraLifeDropChance`) continues to apply and composes with the new
      multiplier without making the curve rise with campaign level.
- [ ] **AC6 — Parity & no duplicate implementation:** the rule exists once in a
      shared module and is consumed by the game and the gyms; the repo-wide
      duplicate-body guard (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`)
      passes.
- [ ] **AC7 — Tests:** unit tests cover the curve (monotonic, 1.0× at full
      lives, exponential at low lives, clamping/guards), the mini-boss
      guarantee (exactly one `extra_life` spawned per defeat, game + gym), and
      the seeded distribution; the changed-scope test gate passes.
- [ ] **AC8 — Documentation:** the GDD §4.4 (Extra Life drop), §3.3.1 /
      §4.4.4 (mini-boss defeat/reward — which today state the sweep is
      cosmetic and the wheel is the single reward) and the game-rules
      documentation/code comments are updated, including any relevant wiki or
      docs-site entries.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Impact

A player who is down to their last life quietly sees Extra Life drops a little
more often — enough to feel lucky, never enough to notice — and every mini-boss
kill now reliably leaves one on the field.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity is mandatory** (`AGENTS.md`; `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`): the rule
  lives once in the shared core and is consumed by `PlayScene` and the relevant
  gym scenes (`GymFormationScene`, `GymMiniBoss`, and any asteroid/level gym
  that rolls Extra Life). No divergent copies.
- **Subtlety is a hard requirement:** the curve must not make Extra Life
  common; the player must not be able to perceive the manipulation.
- **No new art/assets:** reuse the existing `extra_life` code-drawn icon and
  shared drop pipeline.
- **Do not regress the deliberate supply reduction:** AH-0MW3MLTY3005MIXR /
  AH-0MW10ZVLH005IJRM halved the supply dial and turned the asteroid
  Extra-Life roll off. The adaptive uplift must be layered on top, not undo
  that tuning.
- **Extra Life stays field-pickup-only:** it must not leak back onto the
  hold-full choice or the mini-boss wheel (§4.4.4).

## Existing state

- **Generic per-kill drop:** `PlayScene._maybeDropPowerUp()` rolls the
  level-resolved per-kill chance `powerUpDropChance(level, rules)` (0.09 at
  level 1 → 0.025 at level 10), then draws one kind from the shared weighted
  pool via `_drawNextDrop` (`src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts`,
  `CombatCoreScene._buildDefaultDropSpawner`).
- **Extra Life weight:** fixed `DEFAULT_EXTRA_LIFE_WEIGHT = 3` in
  `src/core/rules.ts` (`defaultPowerUpWeights()`), against 4 for standard
  power-ups and 2 for the rare Smart Bomb / Orbital Strike. It never varies
  with lives.
- **Lives:** `GameState.lives` (start 3, cap `MAX_LIVES = 5` from the Extra
  Life catalogue entry). `Player`/HUD read the same value; the scene has
  `this.gameState.lives` at kill time.
- **Asteroid Extra Life roll:** `rollAsteroidExtraLife` +
  `extraLifeDropChance(level, rules)` in `src/scenes/core/asteroidKillDrops.ts`
  — currently **off** (`asteroidExtraLifeDropChance = 0`).
- **Mini-boss defeat:** `PlayScene._damageMiniBoss` → `miniBoss.destroy()` runs
  the cosmetic death sweep (no drops, no score, no telemetry) and opens the
  spin-the-wheel reward (§4.4.4). Extra Life is deliberately excluded from the
  wheel. Consequently a mini-boss kill currently leaves **no** Extra Life.
- **Gym consumers:** `GymFormationScene` (`_rollExtraLifeDrop`), `GymLevel`,
  `GymMiniBoss` — the first two already call the shared asteroid roll; the
  mini-boss gym exercises the reward wheel.

## Desired change

1. Add a shared, pure **life-adaptive Extra Life multiplier** and apply it to
   every Extra Life drop source (at minimum the generic per-kill pool; see Q1
   for whether the asteroid roll also composes with it). At full lives the
   behaviour is byte-for-byte today's; as lives fall the Extra Life probability
   rises on an exponential curve so the player "feels lucky" at 1 life without
   noticing at 2.
2. Make **every mini-boss defeat always spawn one `extra_life` field pickup**
   at/near the death position, on top of the wheel reward, in the game and in
   `GymMiniBoss`.
3. Express both behaviours as named, persisted `GameRules` tunables with
   documented defaults and load-time clamping.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/rules.ts` — add the adaptive-curve tunables (base / reference
  lives / cap) to `GameRules`, defaults, clamping, schema-compatible load.
- `src/core/livesScaling.ts` **(new)** — the pure life→multiplier helper
  (single source of truth), beside `levelScaling.ts`.
- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts` / `CombatCoreScene.ts` — expose the
  Extra-Life weight adjustment through the shared drop draw so game + gyms
  share it.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — apply the multiplier at kill time
  (`_maybeDropPowerUp`) and spawn the guaranteed Extra Life on mini-boss defeat
  (`_damageMiniBoss` / `_finaliseMiniBossDefeat`).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — consume the shared multiplier.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts` — consume the guaranteed mini-boss drop
  (gym has no run lives: unconditional, matching the game's "always").
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/core/livesScaling.test.ts` **(new)**,
  `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.miniboss*.test.ts` — coverage.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 / §3.3.1 / §4.4.4 wording.

## Related work

- **Add an extra life power up (AH-0MT7UX8LE0072MR3)** — introduced P8 Extra
  Life (passive +1, cap 5, rarer than standard drops). Completed.
- **Asteroids drop more lives (AH-0MV6M2M9P0078N4S)** — added the small-asteroid
  Extra-Life roll (`rollAsteroidExtraLife`, `asteroidExtraLifeDropChance`).
  Completed.
- **Use level-resolved power-up drop chance in PlayScene
  (AH-0MVLJF5P0005KF8X)** — wired `powerUpDropChance` / `extraLifeDropChance`
  into the kill path. Completed.
- **Level-scaling curves (AH-0MVLJEE7O008RX9X)** — `src/core/levelScaling.ts`,
  the supply dial this feature composes with.
- **Supply-dial reduction / asteroid roll off (AH-0MW3MLTY3005MIXR,
  AH-0MW10ZVLH005IJRM)** — deliberate supply tightening; do not undo.
- **Mini-boss defeat sweep (AH-0MVOFGB6K003YD0Z)** — cosmetic sweep, no drops.
- **Mini-Boss Reward — Spin the Wheel (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD)** — the encounter's
  current single reward; Extra Life is field-pickup-only and excluded from the
  wheel. The guaranteed drop in this item must not change that exclusion.
- **Bot prioritises extra lives (AH-0MV03GXZQ00801T4)** — the demo brain already
  prefers a live Extra Life pickup below the cap; unaffected but retested.
- **Duplicate check:** no completed item satisfies this brief's ACs. The
  closest completed items (above) implement fixed-rate Extra Life drops and the
  mini-boss reward; neither adapts the rate to lives nor guarantees a
  mini-boss Extra Life. No duplicate found.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Perceptibility risk (highest):** an exponential curve tuned too high is
  noticeable and undermines the "not noticeable" requirement. Mitigation: keep
  the recommended base modest, verify with a seeded statistical test, and keep
  every constant in `GameRules` for retuning.
- **Compounding with level scaling:** the supply dial already lowers drop
  chance with campaign level. The adaptive multiplier must be applied after
  level scaling so a late-campaign player on 1 life still gets a meaningful
  (but still subtle) uplift. See Q3.
- **Double-dipping risk:** if the multiplier is applied to both the generic
  pool weight and an independent asteroid roll, low-life drop rates could stack
  unexpectedly. Q1/Q3 pin this down.
- **Mini-boss drop clutter / cap:** a guaranteed drop at 5 lives is a wasted
  pickup. Assumption: still spawn it ("always" is literal); the six-slot gate
  and life cap handle collection. If the producer prefers "only when below
  cap", that is a scope variant (Q2).
- **Gym semantics:** gyms have no run lives. Assumption: `GymMiniBoss` always
  spawns the drop; other gyms use their own seeded/deterministic life context
  (or full-lives baseline) so parity tests stay deterministic.
- **Scope-creep risk:** do not add a HUD "pity counter", a visible luck meter,
  or extra-life bounties here — record any such idea as a linked work item.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

> Answer each below or reply in-session. Until answered the brief is
> provisional and the item stays flagged for producer review.

- **Q1 — Which drop channel should adapt? (mechanism)**
  - (a) Scale the `extra_life` **weight inside the existing weighted per-kill
    pool** (drop frequency unchanged; Extra Life becomes a larger share of the
    existing drops as lives fall).
  - (b) Add a **separate independent Extra Life roll per kill** (mirrors the
    asteroid rule; adds extra-life drops on top of the existing pool).
  - (c) Raise the **overall per-kill drop chance** when low on lives.
  - **Recommended: (a)** — it is the least noticeable (total power-up frequency
    is untouched) and preserves the tuned supply dial; (b) mildly raises total
    drop frequency when low, and (c) is the most perceptible.
  - **OPEN QUESTION — Answer:** _(none yet)_

- **Q2 — What does "mini-boss kill always leaves an extra life power up" mean
  exactly?**
  - (a) Always spawn a physical `extra_life` **field pickup** at the death
    position, **in addition to** the wheel reward, even at the 5-life cap / full
    slots (existing gate handles collection).
  - (b) Same as (a) but **only when the player is below the life cap**.
  - (c) Add Extra Life as a **wheel wedge/outcome** instead of a field pickup.
  - **Recommended: (a)** — "always" is literal, Extra Life is
    field-pickup-only (so the wheel must stay free of it), and the wheel remains
    the encounter's permanent-upgrade reward.
  - **OPEN QUESTION — Answer:** _(none yet)_

- **Q3 — Curve shape, magnitude, and interaction with level scaling.**
  - (a) `multiplier = base ** livesLost` (recommended base ≈ 2.5–3), applied
    on top of the level-scaled Extra Life probability; 1.0× at starting lives,
    no cap.
  - (b) A gentler/other curve or a producer-supplied per-lives table
    (e.g. 1.0× / 2× / 5×).
  - (c) Also compose the multiplier into the (currently 0) asteroid Extra-Life
    roll so every Extra Life source adapts.
  - **Recommended: (a) with base 3** (≈1× / 3× / 9×) **and (c) yes** — one rule
    for every Extra Life source; base 3 is the smallest that still reads as
    "exponential" while staying subtle. Provide exact numbers if you want a
    specific feel.
  - **OPEN QUESTION — Answer:** _(none yet)_
